name: Eric Lombardi
description: Eric Lombardi is a Toronto-based strategy consultant in financial services and technology, a writer on Ontario's economy and growth, founder of More Neighbours Toronto, and the 2026 Ontario Liberal leadership candidate who published a fully costed platform for the province.
short_description: Strategy consultant in financial services and technology. Writer and advocate on growth, housing and government capability in Ontario.

hero.headline: A future worth building.
hero.lede: I'm a strategy consultant in financial services and technology, and I write and organize for the reforms that help people build secure lives: homes they can afford, useful work, services that function, and more room for the next generation to succeed.
hero.note: Finance and technology entrepreneur turned civic builder. Founder of More Neighbours Toronto. Candidate for Ontario Liberal leader in 2026. Columns in The Hub and the Toronto Star.

pillars.title: Consulting
pillars.text: Strategy, mergers and acquisitions, ventures and delivery for financial services and technology companies, from a two-week decision to a multi-year program.

pillars.title: Writing and media
pillars.text: Essays on growth, housing, infrastructure and government capability, plus columns, interviews and appearances elsewhere.

pillars.title: Public policy
pillars.text: The 2026 Ontario Liberal leadership campaign and its platform, More Neighbours Toronto, and Build Toronto.

form._how: endpoint = the email tool's form-post URL; map its field names in fields; consent = 'statement' (text under the button) or 'checkbox' (CASL-conservative). Empty endpoint = mailto fallback.

analytics._how: simpleanalytics was used on ericforolp.ca. Add ericlombardi.ca in that account, then set enabled: true.

support._how: contribute_url = a pay-what-you-want monthly link (e.g. a Stripe Payment Link with 'customer chooses amount', recurring); one_time_url = the same for a single gift; platform = the name shown to visitors (e.g. Stripe). live: true turns the buttons on.
